messages:

Cc: Priya Ramesh <priya.r@cognira.com>
Date: Sat, 09 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Cognira traffic snapshot + ask: how much headroom should we plan for?

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking an intro call last week. As we discussed, Cognira is evaluating a dedicated GPU pool for our conversational and document-understanding product line. Attached is a 7-day sample of traffic (csv) and a short file with example prompts/responses. High level:
- Peak QPS: ~120 requests/sec (spiky, ~30% within 5 minute bursts)
- Typical prompt length: 150-250 tokens, mean response: 120 tokens
- Mix: 60% short assistant replies, 30% generation-heavy (summaries), 10% embeddings/rerank

Request: we need a quick recommendation for (a) committed GPU count for predictable p99 latency of <300ms for interactive flows and (b) how much buffer/headroom for burst windows and degradation strategy.

Attached: cognira_traffic_sample.csv, sample_prompts_and_responses.txt, initial_sla_request.pdf

Would love a brief pre-sales checklist or playbook items we can share with our infra and procurement by end of next week.

Best,
Alex
Alex Foster
CTO, Cognira
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>

Cc: Priya Ramesh <priya.r@cognira.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 09 May 2026 13:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Cognira traffic snapshot + ask: how much headroom should we plan for?

Alex — thanks for the samples, this is helpful. Quick follow-ups so we can size conservatively and propose a staged commitment: 

1) Concurrency vs request-per-second: can you confirm whether the 120 rps peak is sustained across the full minute or concentrated into 5–15s microbursts? (Your note indicates 30% in 5-min bursts but the CSV granularity matters.)
2) Session affinity: do requests reuse KV cache / ongoing chat sessions? If yes, what fraction of traffic is multi-turn (reuses context) vs stateless single-turn?
3) SLA tolerance: is p99 <300ms the hard requirement for all request types, or just interactive/assistant flows? For embeddings and batch rerank we usually recommend higher latency tolerance.
4) Any regulatory constraints (data residency/KMS) or preferred regions? You noted US but want to confirm.

Marissa — looping you in for the traffic-to-GPU probe. Can you run a preliminary ballpark mapping (A100 / H100 mix) and identify sensible burst buffer (1.5x vs 2x) assumptions given their prompt/response lengths?

Plan: we'll return a 1-page headroom proposal + recommended staged commit (pilot -> commit) and an optional stress-test runbook. Target: initial reply by Tue EOD.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Cognira traffic snapshot + ask: how much headroom should we plan for?

Adding the pre-sales sizing notes inline. Alex / Priya — copying the assumptions so you can validate quickly.

Summary assumptions (from attached samples):
- Avg prompt tokens: 180; avg response tokens: 120; typical model family: Llama3-13B-like (open model).
- Request mix: 60% chat (multi-turn), 30% generation (single-turn long outputs), 10% embeddings/rerank.
- Observed burst pattern: 5–8 minute concentrated windows with 1–2 minute microbursts inside. CSV has 60s granularity; if you can provide 10s granularity we can tighten the buffer.

Ballpark GPU mapping (interactive p99 target <300ms):
- Pilot (non-committed): 4x H100-equivalent nodes (node = 8xA100/4xH100 equivalency depending on vendor). Expected sustained throughput ~60 RPS for interactive flows with p99 ~220–280ms and room for 20–30% microburst before p99 degrades.
- Committed baseline (recommended for 99.9% SLO): 8x H100-equivalents — provides steady-state headroom and lowers unit cost via reserved pricing.
- Burst buffer recommendation: configure autoscale with a 1.8x burst capacity (i.e., be able to temporarily route up to ~1.8 * provisioned slots) and a K/V prefix cache to reduce repeated token compute for multi-turn sessions.

Operational suggestions:
- Enable prefix caching for high-reuse flows (saves ~25–40% token compute in our tests).
- Canary routing: route 10% of traffic to a quantized 8-bit model variant for cost validation during peak windows; fallback to full 16-bit model if quality alerts fire.
- Stress test: we recommend a 90-min spike test (3x peak RPS for 10 minutes repeated every 20 mins) to validate request queuing and cold-start behavior. We'll provide a runbook.

Attachments: sample sizing worksheet (attached here as a stub), stress_test_playbook.md (we'll upload after internal review).

Questions for Cognira:
- Can you share a 10s granularity sample for two representative peak days?
- Any talk of embedding-heavy batch windows that could be shifted to off-peak?

If you confirm the granularity and residency (US), I can convert this into a short commit recommendation (numbers above) and an estimated monthly cost delta with reserved pricing.

—Marissa
